lessons.title: Purpose and use
lessons.html:
This guide condenses the Grade E, D and C training manual into practical learning units for classroom, revision and online study. It must be used with facilitator guidance, current provider procedures and the full training manual where detailed reference is required.

Important: This guide does not replace current law, PSiRA requirements, post orders, emergency instructions or supervised practical training.

lessons.title: How to study each module
lessons.html:
• Read the outcomes before starting.
  • Work through the essential knowledge and ask questions where anything is unclear.
  • Discuss the workplace scenario and relate it to site procedures.
  • Answer the self-check questions without looking back, then verify your response.
  • Complete the matching activity in the Learner Workbook.

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Personal Hygiene and General Appearance

Learning focus: Suggested time: 60 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes
lessons.html:
• Apply personal-hygiene practices appropriate to security work.
  • Explain how grooming and uniform standards affect health and professionalism.
  • Identify hygiene practices that reduce illness and contamination risks.

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Report for duty clean, rested and correctly dressed in a complete uniform.
  • Bathe regularly; keep hands, nails, teeth, hair and feet clean.
  • Wear clean clothing and socks and keep footwear presentable.
  • Use handwashing, ventilation and food hygiene to reduce the spread of illness.
  • Balance work with exercise, rest and sufficient sleep.
Workplace scenario: A colleague arrives for duty in a soiled uniform and appears unwell. Explain a respectful, safety-conscious response.

lessons.title: Check yourself
lessons.html:
1. Why does personal hygiene matter in security work?
  1. Name four daily grooming standards.

Key takeaway: Report for duty clean, rested and correctly dressed in a complete uniform.

chapters.name: Module 03: Role and Function of Security

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Role and Function of Security

Learning focus: Suggested time: 90 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes
lessons.html:
• Explain the role and core functions of security personnel.
  • Distinguish vulnerable areas from vital points.
  • Apply the main principles of security to routine duties.

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Security protects information, material and assets, and people.
  • Apply need-to-know principles to sensitive information.
  • A vulnerable area is relatively easy to penetrate or difficult to observe.
  • A vital point is essential to operations, such as a control room or power supply.
  • Observe, deter, detect, report and support lawful investigation.
Workplace scenario: During patrol you find a damaged fence near the generator room. Identify the vulnerable area, vital point and immediate actions.

Key takeaway: Security protects information, material and assets, and people.

lessons.title: Overview

Recognition of Bombs, Explosive Devices and Firearms

Learning focus: Suggested time: 120 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes
lessons.html:
• Recognise common firearm, explosive-device and bomb-threat indicators.
  • Apply safe notification, isolation and evacuation actions.
  • Record and report bomb-threat information without handling suspicious objects.

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Treat an unusual unattended object as suspicious until assessed by authorised specialists.
  • Do not touch, move, open, cover or closely examine a suspicious object.
  • Move people away, control access and follow the site emergency plan.
  • Notify the control point, supervisor and emergency services through approved channels.
  • During a threat call, remain calm and record the caller’s exact words, time, voice and background sounds.
Workplace scenario: A bag with visible wires is found near an entrance. State the safe sequence of actions and what must not be done.

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Basic Self-Defence and Personal Safety

Learning focus: Suggested time: 90 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes
lessons.html:
• Identify hazards, warning signs and safer positioning.

  • Report and preserve information after a safety incident.

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Prevention, awareness and de-escalation come before physical response.
  • Maintain distance, a safe exit route and access to assistance.
  • Use calm communication and avoid unnecessary confrontation.
  • Use only lawful, necessary and proportionate force within training and authority.
  • After an incident, obtain help, preserve evidence and report promptly.
Workplace scenario: A person is shouting and moving closer while blocking your route. Explain how you would position, communicate and seek help.

Observation

Learning focus: Suggested time: 90 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes
lessons.html:
• Observe people, vehicles and objects systematically.

  • Describe relevant identifying details accurately.

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Use sight, hearing and other safe sensory information purposefully.
  • Observe systematically rather than relying on a quick impression.
  • Record facts: time, location, direction, sequence, appearance and behaviour.
  • Describe people from general to specific and vehicles by make, colour, registration and distinctive features.
  • Avoid guessing; label uncertainty clearly.
Workplace scenario: You see a vehicle leave quickly after an alarm. Record only the observable facts that could assist a follow-up.

Firefighting, Prevention and Protection

Learning focus: Suggested time: 120 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes

• Identify common fire hazards and basic fire-prevention measures.
  • Select safe first actions when smoke or fire is discovered.
  • Support evacuation and access for emergency responders.

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Prevent fire through good housekeeping, safe electrical use and correct storage.
  • Know alarm points, exits, assembly points and emergency contacts.
  • On discovering fire: raise the alarm, protect life, call for help and follow the site plan.
  • Use firefighting equipment only if trained, authorised, the fire is small and escape remains safe.
  • Never use lifts during a fire unless the approved emergency plan specifically permits it.
Workplace scenario: Smoke is coming from an electrical cabinet. State your priorities and explain when you should not attempt firefighting.

Legal Aspects

Learning focus: Suggested time: 180 minutes. Build knowledge, apply it to a realistic situation and record evidence of understanding.

lessons.title: Learning outcomes

lessons.title: Essential knowledge
lessons.html:
• Work only within registration status, training, assignment and lawful authority.
  • Respect dignity, privacy and constitutional rights while protecting people and property.
  • Arrest, search and force have legal limits; uncertainty must be escalated.
  • Force must be necessary, proportionate and discontinued when the threat ends.
  • Record facts, preserve evidence and hand matters to authorised officials.

The Threat

lessons.title: Learning outcomes

lessons.title: Immediate priorities during an incident
lessons.html:
1. Protect life and avoid creating additional danger.
  1. Raise the alarm and request the correct assistance.
  1. Follow post orders, the site emergency plan and lawful instructions.
  1. Control access and preserve the scene or evidence where safe.
  1. Record facts, times, communications and actions promptly.

  • Confirm important details.
  • Avoid rumours and unsupported conclusions.
  • Use authorised channels.
  • Record the message and action taken.

lessons.title: Glossary
lessons.html:
TermMeaning
Access controlMeasures used to regulate and record entry, exit or movement within premises.
De-escalationCommunication and positioning intended to reduce tension and prevent violence.
Occurrence bookAn official chronological record of events, reports and actions at a security site.
PocketbookA security officer’s contemporaneous personal record of duties, observations and actions.
ProportionateAppropriate in degree to the lawful purpose and the risk faced.
Suspicious objectAn unusual or unattended item requiring caution, isolation and escalation.
ThreatA person, act, condition or event with the potential to cause harm or loss.
Vital pointAn asset, location or system whose loss would seriously affect operations.
Vulnerable areaA place relatively exposed to unauthorised access, damage or attack.

lessons.html: When uncertain: Stop, protect safety, preserve rights, control access lawfully, contact the authorised supervisor or relevant authority, and record the decision.

lessons.title: Source hierarchy and controlled updates
lessons.html:
Training material must distinguish binding law from guidance, site instructions and historical source material. When two sources appear inconsistent, do not select the most convenient wording: pause the activity and obtain an authorised interpretation.

PriorityControl question
1. Constitution and legislation in forceApply the current enacted and commenced provisions, as amended.
2. Regulations and lawful statutory instrumentsConfirm that the instrument is final, commenced and applicable to the site and role.
3. Valid appointment, delegation or directiveConfirm the issuer, scope, effective date, territorial limit and any conditions.
4. Approved security policy and planUse the current controlled version approved for the site.
5. Post orders and operating proceduresFollow only lawful, current instructions that fall within the officer's role and competence.
6. Training guides and historical referencesUse to support learning, never as a substitute for current authority.

lessons.title: Status labels used in this guide
lessons.html:
• CURRENT OFFICIAL SOURCE: published by the responsible authority and checked on the review date.
  • TRANSITIONAL: application depends on commencement, designation or a site-specific transition process.
  • DRAFT: published for comment or development and not treated as operative law unless final promulgation is confirmed.
  • HISTORICAL: retained only to explain the legacy unit standard or source guide and requiring verification before operational use.
2023 draft regulations: The Critical Infrastructure Protection Regulations published for public comment in July 2023 are treated here as a draft source. Confirm whether final regulations have since been promulgated before using any draft provision in training or site procedures.

lessons.title: Rights-based operating principles
lessons.html:
Security at a National Key Point must be effective without abandoning legality, dignity, accountability or proportionality. A protected location does not create unlimited authority.

PrincipleApplication
LawfulnessAct only under a current law, valid delegation, approved site instruction or recognised common-law power.
NecessityTake only the action reasonably required to achieve a lawful security purpose.
ProportionalityThe level of restriction or force must match the actual risk and must cease when the need ends.
DignityCommunicate respectfully and conduct any lawful search with privacy, decency and sensitivity.
AccountabilityRecord decisions, actions, property and notifications accurately and promptly.
EscalationRefer uncertain legal questions, serious incidents and contested authority to an authorised supervisor or the police.

lessons.title: Information protection
lessons.html:
• Share protected information only with authorised persons who require it for a lawful purpose.
  • Do not post photographs, diagrams, access arrangements or incidents on social media.
  • Protect paper and electronic records from unauthorised access, alteration, loss or disclosure.
  • Report suspected information loss, espionage, sabotage or unauthorised disclosure immediately through approved channels.

chapters.name: Learning Unit 1: Governance, Authority and Safeguarding Responsibilities

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Functions of the Minister and the owner

Specific outcome: Explain the functions of the Minister and the owner or responsible person in relation to a National Key Point.

lessons.title: Assessment focus
lessons.html:
• Explain key terms within the applicable legal framework.
  • Describe the Minister's or delegated authority's principal functions.
  • Describe the owner's governance, resourcing and safeguarding responsibilities.
  • Explain how site security roles support the approved security system.

lessons.title: Core terminology
lessons.html:
TermWorking meaning
National Key PointA place or area declared under the applicable National Key Points legislation. Confirm current legal status and designation.
Critical infrastructureInfrastructure considered under the Critical Infrastructure Protection Act framework. Do not assume that every National Key Point has automatically completed the new declaration process.
Owner / person in controlThe person or entity with legal control or responsibility for the site and its safeguarding obligations.
Protecting authority or forceA public authority or force assigned a role under the applicable law, designation or approved plan.
Security limitA defined and properly communicated boundary relevant to the security controls of the protected site.
IncidentAn occurrence or threat that may prejudicially affect the security, operation, people, information or assets of the protected site.

lessons.title: Minister or delegated authority
lessons.html:
• Exercise statutory functions only within the legislation currently in force.
  • Issue lawful notices, directions, standards or delegations through prescribed processes.
  • Receive information and oversee compliance where legislation authorises this.
  • Coordinate with the appropriate government, policing and defence structures.

lessons.title: Owner or person in control
lessons.html:
• Establish and maintain an approved security policy and security plan.
  • Provide adequate trained personnel, supervision, equipment and facilities.
  • Control authorised access and movement of persons, goods and vehicles.
  • Prevent, detect, report and manage incidents through approved procedures.
  • Maintain occurrence books, registers, appointment records and security evidence.
  • Review risks, conduct exercises and correct deficiencies identified through inspection or incident review.

lessons.title: Operational security structure
lessons.html:
LevelPrimary contribution
Strategic governanceMinister or statutory authority; owner or person in control; approved oversight structures.
Security managementSecurity manager or chief security officer; policies, plans, resources, liaison and assurance.
Shift controlControl security officer or authorised supervisor; deployment, communications, escalation and records.
Front-line deliveryAuthorised security personnel; access control, patrol, observation, response and reporting.
External supportSouth African Police Service, emergency services and other protecting forces or authorities where applicable.

lessons.title: Ministerial, delegated and oversight functions
lessons.html:
The legacy guide reproduced extensive extracts about ministerial powers. This edition restores the learning purpose in a controlled form: learners must understand what a statutory decision can affect, while confirming the exact current provision before acting on it.

FunctionLearner understanding
Designation or declarationA formal decision may identify a protected site and establish the legal framework that applies to it.
Information and assessmentAuthorised structures may require information, conduct assessments or consider security risk within the power granted by law.
Directions and conditionsLawful directions or conditions may define required protective measures, responsibilities or reporting arrangements.
DelegationA delegate may exercise only the function lawfully delegated and only within its stated scope and conditions.
Entry and inspectionEntry, inspection or information-gathering powers must be exercised by an authorised person under the applicable legal conditions.
CoordinationThe responsible authority may coordinate government, policing, defence, emergency and owner structures where the current framework provides for this.

lessons.title: Check a claimed statutory instruction
lessons.html:
1. Identify the person or office issuing the instruction.
  1. Confirm the legal provision, delegation or written authority relied upon.
  1. Check the site, subject matter, effective date and conditions covered.
  1. Record the instruction and escalate any inconsistency or uncertainty.

lessons.title: Owner safeguarding system
lessons.html:
The owner or person in control carries strategic responsibilities that cannot be shifted entirely to an individual security officer or contractor. Contracting a service does not remove the need for governance, resources, assurance and corrective action.

Control areaOwner-level responsibility
GovernanceApprove responsibilities, decision rights, reporting lines and review arrangements.
Security policy and planMaintain controlled documents based on current law, risk assessment and approved protective measures.
PeopleAppoint suitable personnel, define roles, verify competence and provide supervision.
Equipment and facilitiesProvide serviceable communications, protective equipment, identification, keys, registers and facilities required for lawful duties.
Access and movementDefine authorisation, identification, search conditions, visitor controls and escalation routes.
Incident managementEnable notification, command, emergency response, evidence protection, recovery and learning.
AssuranceInspect, test, exercise and review the system; assign and close corrective actions.

lessons.title: Records that demonstrate control
lessons.html:
• approved policy, security plan, post orders and version history;
  • appointments, screening, competence, induction and refresher records;
  • equipment issue, maintenance, key and credential registers;
  • occurrence books, patrol records, incident reports and escalation logs; and
  • inspection findings, exercise reports, corrective actions and management reviews.

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Recruitment, selection and training

Specific outcome: Explain the recruitment, selection, appointment and training requirements applicable to National Key Point security personnel.

lessons.title: Assessment focus
lessons.html:
• Explain why identity, history, competence and suitability information is required.
  • Identify disqualifying or risk factors that must be assessed lawfully.
  • Explain provisional appointment controls without assuming a universal time period.
  • Describe initial, site-specific and refresher training requirements.

lessons.title: Fair and lawful recruitment
lessons.html: Recruitment must protect the site while respecting employment law, privacy, equality and fair procedure. Only information authorised by law or genuinely required for the role should be collected.

lessons.title: Information commonly verified
lessons.html:
• Identity, citizenship or lawful work status and current contact details.
  • Employment history, references and relevant qualifications.
  • Security-industry registration and good standing where required.
  • Criminal-record or integrity screening through lawful and authorised processes.
  • Fitness, competence and licences relevant to the assigned duties.
  • Conflicts of interest, prior security incidents or other declared risks relevant to the role.
Data protection: Collect only necessary information, explain its purpose, restrict access, keep it accurate and retain it only for an authorised period.

lessons.title: Appointment and competence controls
lessons.html:
StageRequired control
Before appointmentVerify identity, authority to work, registration, role requirements, screening outcome and required competence.
Provisional appointmentUse only where current law and approved provider or site processes allow it. Define supervision, restricted duties, training deadline and review date in writing.
Certificate or appointment recordIssue, control and withdraw the relevant site or statutory credential through the authorised process.
DeploymentConfirm that the person is trained, equipped, briefed and authorised for the assigned post.
Ongoing suitabilityMonitor conduct, competence, registration, licence status, refresher training and changes that may affect deployment.

lessons.title: Disqualification and risk decisions
lessons.html:
Do not rely on the legacy guide's historic list without review. Current legislation, regulations, employer policy and fair labour practices must determine the decision. The applicant or employee should be treated consistently and given the process required by law and policy.

  • Record the verified fact, the applicable requirement and the authorised decision-maker.
  • Distinguish automatic legal disqualification from a risk that requires assessment.
  • Do not discriminate on an irrelevant or prohibited ground.
  • Protect screening information and communicate the outcome only to authorised parties.

lessons.title: Application and appointment file
lessons.html:
The legacy guide listed detailed application particulars. The current control objective is to establish identity, lawful eligibility, suitability, competence and an auditable appointment decision without collecting irrelevant personal information.

File componentEvidence required
Identity and contactVerified identity, lawful work status and reliable contact details.
Employment and referencesRelevant work history, explanations for material gaps and references checked through an authorised process.
Regulatory standingCurrent security-industry registration and any role-specific licence or authorisation.
Integrity and risk screeningLawfully obtained screening results assessed against current requirements and fair procedure.
Health and fitnessOnly role-relevant information obtained through a lawful and confidential process.
Qualifications and competenceVerified certificates, training results and demonstrated competence for assigned duties.
Decision recordAuthorised approval, restrictions, conditions, review date and reasons recorded.

lessons.title: Information-quality controls
lessons.html:
• Verify documents with the issuing source where required.
  • Resolve inconsistencies before appointment or deployment.
  • Restrict access to screening and medical information.
  • Record corrections and retention or disposal decisions.

lessons.title: Appointment, credential and competence lifecycle
lessons.html:
Lifecycle stageMinimum control
1. SelectApply lawful criteria consistently and document the decision.
2. AppointIssue a written appointment or contract that defines role, authority, conditions and reporting line.
3. InductComplete general and site-specific induction before unsupervised duty.
4. AuthoriseIssue only the credentials, keys, systems access and equipment required for the role.
5. DeployConfirm competence, briefing, fitness for duty and post authorisation at each assignment.
6. MonitorReview conduct, performance, training, registration, licences and restrictions.
7. Refresh or remediateProvide training after change, incident, error, absence or identified competence gap.
8. Suspend, withdraw or closeRemove access and equipment promptly when authority ends or risk requires action; preserve the audit record.

lessons.title: Provisional employment
lessons.html:
A provisional appointment is not permission for unrestricted deployment. Where current law and approved procedures allow it, the record must state the legal basis, restricted duties, supervision, outstanding checks, required training, review date and authorised decision-maker.

Credential control: A card, certificate or uniform does not create authority by itself. Authority depends on the current legal framework, valid appointment, assigned role, competence and site authorisation.

lessons.title: Training programme
lessons.html:
• Foundational security competence and current regulatory requirements.
  • National Key Point legal framework and the current transition to critical-infrastructure legislation.
  • Site induction, post orders, boundaries, access control and information protection.
  • Observation, communication, occurrence-book entries and incident reporting.
  • Emergency procedures, evacuation, fire safety and first-response responsibilities.
  • Lawful search, arrest, evidence protection and use-of-force decision-making.
  • Equipment training delivered only by appropriately qualified persons.

lessons.title: Refresher and remedial training
lessons.html: Refresh competence at the intervals required by current law, regulator, site risk and provider policy. Additional training should follow legal change, new equipment, role change, incident findings, poor performance or an extended absence from a duty.

lessons.title: Selection and training case study
lessons.html:
Activity: Apply the controls above to a fictional candidate.

1. The candidate is registered and experienced but has not completed site-specific training. Decide whether and how the candidate may be deployed.

2. List the documents that must be verified and the persons authorised to approve deployment.

3. Design a short refresher plan after an access-control error revealed a knowledge gap.

lessons.title: Knowledge check
lessons.html:
1. Why must screening information be limited to what is lawful and relevant?

2. What controls are required for any provisional appointment?

3. Name four events that should trigger refresher or remedial training.

chapters.name: Learning Unit 3: Responsibilities, Powers and Limitations

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Responsibilities, powers and limitations

Specific outcome: Explain how the responsibilities, powers and limitations of security personnel are applied lawfully at a National Key Point.

lessons.title: Assessment focus
lessons.html:
• Explain front-line security responsibilities.
  • Apply safe procedures to unidentified persons and unattended articles.
  • Explain consent, authority, privacy and recording requirements for searches.
  • Explain arrest, evidence protection and use-of-force principles.
  • Recognise the territorial, legal and organisational limits of authority.

lessons.title: Responsibilities of security personnel
lessons.html:
• Control authorised movement through assigned access points and security limits.
  • Observe and patrol systematically without creating predictable or unsafe patterns.
  • Prevent and report actions that may prejudice the security of the site.
  • Respond to incidents within training, authority and the approved security plan.
  • Protect people, information, assets, records and possible evidence.
  • Carry out lawful instructions and question or escalate instructions that appear unlawful or unsafe.
  • Maintain professional communication and complete accurate records.
Authority check: Before restricting a person, searching property, seizing an article, making an arrest or using force, identify the exact lawful authority and the limits attached to it.

lessons.title: Safe decision sequence
lessons.html:
1. Observe from a safe position and assess immediate danger.
  1. Identify yourself and request the person's identity, purpose and authority where it is safe and lawful to do so.
  1. Verify the information through the approved access-control process.
  1. Do not grant access while authority remains unconfirmed.
  1. Explain the decision calmly and provide the approved next step.
  1. Call the control point, supervisor or police when risk, refusal or suspected crime requires escalation.
  1. Record the time, place, identity details offered, verification, decision, notifications and outcome.

lessons.title: Important distinction
lessons.html:
IdentityWho the person is.
AuthorityWhy the person may enter, remain or perform a particular activity.
Access conditionsThe escort, pass, search, area, time or other limits attached to entry.

lessons.title: Access-control decision and record
lessons.html:
A security officer must separate observation from assumption. Record what was seen, said, checked and decided; do not label a person suspicious merely because identity or authority has not yet been confirmed.

Record fieldRequired information
Initial observationTime, place, direction of travel, behaviour and any immediate safety concern.
Information requestedIdentity, organisation, host, purpose, appointment, vehicle or delivery details as authorised by procedure.
VerificationSystem, register, host or authorised person consulted and the result obtained.
DecisionAccess granted, conditionally granted, delayed, refused or referred; include the lawful or procedural basis.
CommunicationExplanation given to the person and instructions received from control or supervision.
EscalationSupervisor, police or emergency service notified; time, person contacted and response.
ClosureFinal outcome, escort or departure details, record reference and outstanding follow-up.

lessons.title: Communication model
lessons.html:
1. State your role and the access requirement calmly.
  1. Ask one clear question at a time and listen to the response.
  1. Explain what can be verified and what cannot yet be authorised.
  1. Offer the approved next step without arguing or making threats.
  1. Escalate early if behaviour, information or risk changes.

lessons.title: Unattended and suspicious articles
lessons.html: An unattended article must be assessed according to site procedures. If indicators create suspicion of an explosive, incendiary, hazardous or malicious device, do not touch, move, open, cover or closely inspect it.

lessons.title: Immediate priorities
lessons.html:
• Protect life and move people away using the approved emergency plan.
  • Control access without approaching the object unnecessarily.
  • Notify the control point, supervisor and emergency services through approved channels.
  • Avoid radio, phone or equipment use close to the object if site instructions prohibit it.
  • Record observations from a safe position and preserve the area for authorised specialists.
Do not render harmless: Only authorised bomb-disposal, explosive-ordnance or other qualified specialists may render a suspected device harmless. A security officer protects people and the scene.

lessons.title: Searches, examination and consent
lessons.html: The legal basis for a search must be identified before it begins. Site rules alone do not create unlimited search powers. The exact procedure depends on current legislation, consent, contractual access conditions, arrest powers and approved site directives.

lessons.title: Before a search
lessons.html:
• Confirm who is authorised to conduct the search and the legal basis relied upon.
  • Explain the purpose and procedure in clear language.
  • Obtain valid consent where consent is the basis; consent must be voluntary and may be withdrawn.
  • Use a person of an appropriate gender and a private setting where required by law and policy.
  • Use the least intrusive lawful method and protect dignity and property.
  • Arrange a witness or supervisor where required.

lessons.title: If consent is withdrawn
lessons.html:
• Stop the consent-based search unless a separate lawful authority clearly applies.
  • Do not use force merely to complete a consent-based search.
  • Apply the lawful access consequence, such as refusing entry, and contact the authorised supervisor.
  • Record the withdrawal, response, persons consulted and outcome.

lessons.title: Seizure, property and evidence
lessons.html: An article may be taken only under a lawful power, valid consent or an approved process that is legally authorised. The officer must be able to explain the authority, reason and chain of custody.

lessons.title: Evidence-protection sequence
lessons.html:
1. Protect safety and prevent unnecessary handling or contamination.
  1. Record the article's location, condition and identifying features.
  1. Identify the lawful reason for taking control of it.
  1. Use appropriate packaging, labels and seals where trained and authorised.
  1. Record every transfer, including names, times, signatures and destination.
  1. Hand the item to the authorised supervisor, police or evidence custodian without avoidable delay.
Never: Never keep, use, alter, display or dispose of an article for personal convenience. Never insert missing facts into a record after the event without a transparent correction process.

lessons.title: Search, seizure and property record
lessons.html:
The following record supports accountability but does not create a power to search or seize. Complete it only after the lawful basis and approved procedure have been confirmed.

Record fieldMinimum entry
AuthorityCurrent legal provision, valid consent, arrest-related power or other approved lawful basis.
Person and locationIdentity details offered, role, access point or exact location, date and time.
Explanation and consentWhat was explained, language or assistance used, consent given or refused, and any withdrawal.
Method and safeguardsOfficer, witness, privacy arrangements, scope of search and measures used to protect dignity and property.
Article identifiedObjective description, location found, condition, quantity, serial or identifying marks where safe.
Reason for controlFacts supporting the decision to refuse entry, isolate, retain, seize or refer the article.
ContinuityPackaging or seal reference, each custodian, transfer time, destination and signatures.
Notifications and outcomeSupervisor, police or specialist contacted; instructions, final disposition and report reference.

lessons.title: Property protections
lessons.html:
• Handle only as much as safety, law and evidence protection require.
  • Do not mix personal property from different people or incidents.
  • Record damage, contamination, opening or disposal and the authority for it.
  • Provide a receipt or acknowledgement where the applicable procedure requires one.

lessons.title: Arrest and handover
lessons.html: An arrest is a serious interference with liberty. A security officer must identify a lawful arrest power, communicate the arrest where safe, use only necessary force and arrange prompt handover to the South African Police Service.

lessons.title: Decision questions
lessons.html:
• What offence or legal ground is reasonably suspected?
  • Does the officer have a lawful power to arrest in these circumstances?
  • Is arrest necessary, or can the risk be managed lawfully in another way?
  • What safety risks exist to the person, officer and public?
  • What assistance, medical care, supervisor or police response is required?
  • What facts and actions must be recorded?

lessons.title: After arrest
lessons.html:
• Search an arrested person only under current legal authority and approved procedure.
  • Protect the person's dignity, health and safety.
  • Do not question or punish the person beyond what the law and procedure permit.
  • Record the grounds, time, place, force used, property, injuries, witnesses and notifications.
  • Transfer the person and relevant evidence to the police without unnecessary delay.

lessons.title: Use of force
lessons.html: High-risk topic: This guide provides decision principles, not firearms or physical-intervention instruction. Practical training must be delivered only by authorised, appropriately qualified instructors under current law and approved standards.

lessons.title: Core principles
lessons.html:
PrincipleMeaning
Lawful purposeForce may never be used to punish, intimidate, obtain compliance with an unlawful instruction or protect pride.
NecessityUse force only when a lawful objective cannot reasonably be achieved through a safer means.
ReasonablenessThe response must be one a reasonable person could justify in the actual circumstances known at the time.
ProportionalityThe force must not exceed what is required by the threat or resistance.
CessationReduce or stop force immediately when the lawful need reduces or ends.
Care and reportingObtain medical help where required, preserve evidence and report every use of force accurately.

lessons.title: Firearms
lessons.html: Possession and use of a firearm require the licences, authorisations, competence, issue controls and training prescribed by current law and site policy. A firearm is not a routine compliance tool. Any use or threatened use must satisfy the current legal test and be reported immediately.

lessons.title: Arrest, force and handover reporting
lessons.html:
A complete report must allow an independent reviewer to understand the legal basis, necessity, sequence and outcome. It must record facts known at the time, not a later justification created after the event.

Report sectionRequired content
Ground and authoritySuspected offence or other ground, objective facts, power relied upon and territorial connection.
CommunicationIdentification of officer, words used to communicate arrest or restriction, warnings and responses.
Alternatives consideredWhy observation, access refusal, containment, disengagement or police intervention was or was not sufficient.
Force usedEach action, duration, resistance or threat, equipment involved and when force reduced or stopped.
Health and dignityVisible condition, complaint or injury, restraint checks, medical assistance and privacy safeguards.
Search and propertyAuthority, method, property found, inventory, packaging and continuity record.
HandoverReceiving SAPS member or authorised person, time, place, documents, property and condition at transfer.
ReviewSupervisor notified, incident number, witnesses or recordings preserved and follow-up assigned.
Accuracy: Never coordinate accounts, omit an error or alter a contemporaneous entry. Correct mistakes transparently according to the record-control procedure.

lessons.title: Firearm-specific reporting
lessons.html: Any display, threatened use, discharge, loss or unauthorised access involving a firearm must be handled under current firearms law, regulator requirements, site instructions and the organisation's approved reporting and investigation process.

lessons.title: Limits of authority
lessons.html:
• Territorial limit: special site-related authority does not automatically apply away from the protected site or its legally defined vicinity.
  • Role limit: an officer may act only within current appointment, competence and delegation.
  • Purpose limit: powers may be used only for the lawful security purpose for which they exist.
  • Rights limit: dignity, privacy, bodily integrity, property and liberty remain protected by law.
  • Time limit: restrictions and force must end when the lawful need ends.
  • Evidence limit: suspicion must be based on objective facts, not bias, rumour or a desire to secure a confession.

lessons.title: Escalate when
lessons.html:
• authority is unclear or disputed;
  • a person refuses a search or access condition;
  • a suspected crime, weapon, explosive device or serious threat is involved;
  • force has been used or injury is reported;
  • a site instruction appears unlawful, unsafe or outside the officer's training; or
  • protected information or evidence may have been compromised.

lessons.title: Scenario practice
lessons.html:
Activity: For each scenario, state the authority, safest action, communication, escalation and record required.

1. A contractor has valid identification but no confirmed appointment and demands immediate entry.

2. A visitor withdraws consent after a bag search has started. No other search authority has been confirmed.

3. An unattended backpack with visible wires is found near a busy entrance.

4. During patrol you find an open door, fresh tool marks and a failed light near a restricted area.

lessons.title: Knowledge check
lessons.html:
1. Differentiate identity, authority and access conditions.

2. What must happen when consent to a search is withdrawn?

3. List six principles or controls relevant to lawful use of force.

4. What information must be recorded after an arrest or seizure?

chapters.name: Learning Unit 4: Prohibited Acts, Misconduct and Offences

lessons.title: Overview
lessons.html:
Prohibited acts, misconduct and offences

Specific outcome: Identify prohibited conduct, disciplinary misconduct and offences relevant to safeguarding a National Key Point.

lessons.title: Assessment focus
lessons.html:
• Distinguish workplace misconduct from a criminal offence.
  • Identify conduct that may compromise the security of the site.
  • Explain confidentiality and authorised disclosure.
  • Apply fair reporting, investigation and disciplinary processes.

lessons.title: Misconduct that threatens security
lessons.html:
• Deliberately disobeying a lawful and reasonable security instruction.
  • Sleeping on duty, abandoning a post or failing to perform an assigned control.
  • Reporting for duty impaired by alcohol, drugs, fatigue or another condition that creates risk.
  • Accepting a benefit to bypass an access, search, patrol or reporting requirement.
  • Falsifying, destroying, backdating or concealing security records.
  • Unauthorised disclosure of security measures, incidents, vulnerabilities or protected information.
  • Misusing weapons, equipment, credentials, surveillance systems or personal information.
  • Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, assault, theft or other unlawful conduct.
Fair process: Serious allegations must be reported and investigated through the employer's current disciplinary process. The guide does not itself determine dismissal or criminal guilt.

lessons.title: Disciplinary allegations and fair process
lessons.html:
The legacy guide presented some conduct as automatically resulting in summary dismissal. This edition restores the misconduct topics but separates urgent risk control from the employment decision. Immediate removal from a post may be necessary for safety; dismissal still requires the current lawful and fair process.

StageControl
Secure the operationProtect people, access, information, equipment and evidence; arrange safe relief where necessary.
Report the allegationNotify the authorised manager through the prescribed confidential channel.
Preserve factsKeep occurrence-book entries, system records, video, witness details and relevant property without alteration.
Separate decisionsDistinguish temporary operational restrictions, disciplinary investigation and possible criminal referral.
Apply fair procedureGive notice, an opportunity to respond and the representation or assistance required by current law and policy.
Use an authorised decision-makerAvoid conflicts of interest and base findings on reliable evidence.
Record outcome and follow-upDocument the decision, access or credential changes, appeal or review rights and corrective action.

lessons.title: Potentially serious conduct
lessons.html:
• deliberate security breach, sabotage, theft, corruption or unauthorised disclosure;
  • absence, sleeping, impairment or abandonment that creates a material security risk;
  • dishonesty in an application, security record, incident report or investigation;
  • unlawful violence, intimidation, harassment or misuse of a weapon; and
  • knowing performance of duties while legally disqualified or unauthorised.
Do not predetermine: The seriousness of an allegation does not remove the need to verify facts and apply the appropriate procedure.

lessons.title: Offences and protected information
lessons.html: Conduct may be both workplace misconduct and a criminal offence. The applicable offence, penalty and arrest power must be confirmed from the current legislation rather than copied from historic penalty figures.

lessons.title: Examples requiring immediate escalation
lessons.html:
• Unauthorised entry or remaining within a protected area.
  • Sabotage, terrorism, espionage, malicious damage or credible preparation for such conduct.
  • Obstruction of a person lawfully carrying out statutory safeguarding duties.
  • Theft, fraud, corruption, unauthorised possession of credentials or interference with security systems.
  • Unauthorised disclosure of security measures, incidents or information protected by law or policy.
  • Possession of a prohibited or dangerous object in circumstances creating a security risk.

lessons.title: Authorised disclosure test
lessons.html:
1. Is there a lawful duty or authority to disclose?
  1. Is the recipient authorised and is the information required for a legitimate purpose?
  1. Can the purpose be achieved by sharing less information?
  1. Is the channel approved and secure?
  1. Must the disclosure be recorded or reported?

lessons.title: Conduct and confidentiality
lessons.html:
Activity: Decide whether each case is poor practice, disciplinary misconduct, a suspected offence or more than one. Give reasons and the required escalation.

1. An officer photographs a restricted access point and shares it in a private social-media group.

2. A colleague changes an occurrence-book time to hide a late patrol.

3. A visitor offers money to avoid an access-control requirement.

4. An officer reports a suspected vulnerability through the authorised confidential channel.

lessons.title: Knowledge check
lessons.html:
1. Why can the same conduct be both misconduct and a criminal offence?

2. List five questions that should be asked before protected information is disclosed.

3. Why should historic penalty figures not be copied into a current learner guide without verification?

lessons.title: Integrated formative assessment
lessons.html:
Complete all questions. Your facilitator will provide feedback against the approved assessment plan.

1. Explain the difference between an owner's strategic responsibility and a security officer's operational responsibility.

2. Describe the checks required before a person is deployed to a protected post.

3. State the safe sequence for dealing with an unidentified person at an access point.

4. Explain the lawful response when consent to a search is withdrawn.

5. List the steps required to protect and transfer possible evidence.

6. Explain necessity and proportionality in relation to use of force.

7. Identify four limits on a security officer's authority.

8. Give four examples of conduct that must be reported immediately.

lessons.title: Integrated workplace scenario
lessons.html:
Scenario: At 22:15, a patrol officer finds a rear access door open, fresh marks near the lock and a failed perimeter light. No authorised work is recorded. A person without confirmed authority is seen walking away from the area.

1. State the officer's immediate safety and scene-control actions.

2. Explain how the person's identity and authority should be addressed.

3. Identify who must be notified and what information should be communicated.

4. Describe how possible evidence should be protected.

5. Draft the key facts for the occurrence book and incident report.

2026 UPDATE AND APPLIED-PRACTICE PACK

Edition 3.0 adds current-status controls and deeper workplace practice while preserving the four outcomes of SAQA Unit Standard 246693. All examples are fictional and deliberately exclude real National Key Point layouts, vulnerabilities, codes and response times.

lessons.title: Current official status checked 19 August 2026
lessons.html:
SAQA continues to record Unit Standard 246693 as having passed its registration end date, with 30 June 2029 as the last date for enrolment and 30 June 2032 as the last date for achievement.

The official South African Government Act page lists specified sections of the Critical Infrastructure Protection Act 8 of 2019 as commenced on 30 April 2022. Delivery must still confirm the provisions in force and the site's legal designation on the training date.

The Critical Infrastructure Protection Regulations published for comment in 2023 must be treated as draft unless final promulgation is confirmed in an official Government Gazette before delivery.

Provider scope, learner enrolment, assessor and moderation arrangements, PSiRA standing and site instruments must be validated before each offering.

lessons.title: Core practice themes retained in Edition 4.1
lessons.html:
cyber-physical disruption, social engineering and continuity of access controls;

personal-information minimisation and confidential recruitment records;

insider-risk indicators, protected reporting and fair process;

digital and physical evidence preservation, audit trails and transparent corrections; and

scenario-based decision-making that identifies authority, limits, safety, escalation and records.

The official government record shows selected Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020 provisions commenced on 1 December 2021. Cyber-physical incidents in this guide therefore emphasise safe continuity, minimal disclosure, preservation and authorised reporting; they do not create investigative powers for security officers.

lessons.title: How to use the practical scenarios
lessons.html:
Attempt the learner task before reading the model response.

Use fictional names and locations; never place protected operational information in an online discussion or assignment.

Submit the decision, communication, escalation and record you would use, then compare it with the model response.

A facilitator or assessor must evaluate practical competence; reading a model answer is not proof of competence.

Practical decision model: authority -> limits -> safety -> communication -> escalation -> record.

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 1: An outdated instruction conflicts with the approved plan

Learning Unit 1 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A supervisor produces an old printed instruction that allows deliveries through a side gate after hours. The controlled security plan and current post order require main-gate verification. The supervisor says the old arrangement is faster and instructs the officer to use it immediately.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify the source, version, issuer and authority that must be verified.

Explain how the officer can protect the operation without being argumentative.

State the escalation and record required before the instruction is followed.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Maintain the current approved control while the conflict is checked; urgency does not make an obsolete instruction valid.

Ask the supervisor for the document reference and contact the authorised control point or security manager through an approved channel.

Compare the effective dates, scope and approval record of the documents without circulating protected content unnecessarily.

Follow the confirmed current instruction and record the request, verification, decision-maker, time and operational outcome.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner applies the source hierarchy and version-control principle.

The learner continues lawful security coverage while seeking clarification.

The record is factual and identifies the authorised decision-maker.

Online reflection: What evidence would show that an instruction is current, authorised and applicable to this post?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 2: A repeated gate-system failure remains unresolved

Learning Unit 1 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: The vehicle gate has failed three times in two weeks. Officers have reported each failure, but the corrective-action register has no owner or due date. During the latest failure, vehicles are queuing and a manager asks officers to wave known drivers through without verification.

Training visual: governance review of recurring security-control failures.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Separate the immediate operational response from the owner-level corrective action.

Identify safe temporary controls and the authority needed to approve them.

List the records required to demonstrate reporting, assignment, repair and closure.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Do not abandon identity and authority checks; apply the approved contingency procedure and request additional support if needed.

Notify control and the security manager, record the system status and obtain an authorised temporary-control decision.

Manage the queue safely, communicate delays respectfully and prevent tailgating or informal exceptions.

Link occurrence-book entries, fault reports, maintenance evidence, risk decisions, corrective-action ownership and closure testing.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
Immediate controls preserve access integrity and public safety.

Governance responsibility is not shifted to the gate officer.

Corrective action has an owner, priority, due date and verified closure.

Online reflection: Why is repeated failure a governance issue, not only a maintenance issue?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 3: Candidate records, privacy and deployment readiness

Learning Unit 2 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A candidate has current industry registration and relevant experience. One reference is still outstanding, the site induction has not been completed and a medical form contains information unrelated to the role. Operations want the candidate deployed tonight.

Training visual: identity verification and controlled induction records.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify which information is relevant, who may access it and what remains outstanding.

Decide whether unsupervised deployment is supported by the complete control set.

Explain how the decision and personal information must be protected and recorded.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Restrict the file to authorised recruitment, risk and management personnel and remove or segregate irrelevant medical detail under the approved process.

Verify the outstanding role-relevant reference and complete the required site induction and post assessment before unsupervised deployment.

If an authorised provisional route exists, define restricted duties, supervision, outstanding checks, training deadline and review date in writing.

Record the authorised decision and reasons without copying sensitive information into general occurrence records.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner applies data minimisation and confidentiality.

Registration alone is not treated as proof of site competence.

The deployment decision is authorised, conditional where necessary and auditable.

Online reflection: Which records prove competence without exposing unnecessary personal information?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 4: Provisional appointment under operational pressure

Learning Unit 2 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A new employee has completed foundational training but is awaiting one authorised screening result. A shift is short-staffed, and a manager proposes placing the employee alone at a high-risk access point because the employee already has a uniform and temporary card.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Explain why a uniform or temporary credential does not create authority.

Identify the legal, policy and risk checks required for any provisional appointment.

Design a safe restricted-duty option if the authorised process permits one.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Confirm that provisional appointment is permitted by the current framework and approved provider or site process.

Do not deploy the employee alone to a role requiring checks, competence or authority that remain incomplete.

If permitted, assign only documented low-risk duties under named supervision, with restricted access and equipment.

Record the outstanding check, decision-maker, restrictions, review date and condition that ends provisional status.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner distinguishes staffing pressure from lawful authority.

Restrictions match the unresolved risk and are communicated clearly.

Review and withdrawal controls are documented.

Online reflection: What could go wrong if temporary access is treated as permanent authority?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 5: Refresher training after credential sharing

Learning Unit 2 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: During an access-control system outage, two experienced officers shared one credential to speed up manual processing. No unauthorised entry is confirmed, but the audit trail is unreliable and both officers say the shortcut was necessary.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify the competence, conduct and system-control issues.

Propose immediate risk controls and a proportionate remedial-training plan.

State how competence should be reassessed before normal authority is restored.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Stop credential sharing, preserve the electronic and manual records, and apply the approved outage procedure.

Determine whether the cause was a knowledge gap, inadequate procedure, poor supervision, workload pressure or deliberate misconduct.

Refresh individual credential control, manual verification, outage registers, escalation and handover duties through scenario practice.

Observe each officer completing the procedure correctly and record the reassessment, feedback and any continuing restriction.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The response protects the audit trail and does not assume motive.

Training addresses the demonstrated gap and operating conditions.

Competence is demonstrated, not merely acknowledged by signature.

Online reflection: How can a system weakness create a human shortcut, and how should both be corrected?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 6: Contractor has identification but no confirmed authority

Learning Unit 3 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A contractor presents valid identification and a company card but is not on the appointment list. The contractor says a senior manager is waiting inside and warns that production will stop if access is delayed. A colleague suggests granting entry because the contractor visited last week.

Training visual: verify appointment and authority before granting access.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Distinguish identity, authority and access conditions.

Demonstrate a calm explanation and verification process.

State the escalation and occurrence-book entry required.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Acknowledge the identification but explain that identity does not prove a current appointment or area authorisation.

Keep access controlled while contacting the host or authorised control point using a verified number, not contact details supplied only by the visitor.

Offer the approved waiting or rescheduling process and escalate pressure or disputed instructions to the supervisor.

Record the time, identity details offered, verification sources, decision, communication and final outcome objectively.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
No access is granted on familiarity, status or urgency alone.

Communication is respectful and non-discriminatory.

The learner preserves a complete decision record.

Online reflection: Which verification channel is safest when the visitor supplies the contact number?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 7: Consent is withdrawn during a bag search

Learning Unit 3 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A visitor voluntarily agrees to a bag search as a condition of entry. Halfway through, the visitor withdraws consent, closes the bag and asks to leave. No arrest has occurred and no separate statutory search power has been confirmed.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
State the immediate response to the withdrawal of consent.

Explain the difference between refusing entry and forcing completion of the search.

Identify the communication, escalation and record required.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Stop the consent-based search unless a separate lawful authority clearly applies.

Do not use force merely to complete the search; calmly explain the approved access consequence, which may include refusing entry.

Allow departure unless lawful grounds justify another action, while maintaining safety and contacting the authorised supervisor where required.

Record what was explained, consent given and withdrawn, items already observed without further intrusion, persons consulted and outcome.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner recognises the limits of consent-based authority.

Dignity, property and freedom of movement are respected.

The report separates observation from suspicion or conclusion.

Online reflection: What facts would require police or supervisor involvement without creating a power that does not exist?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 8: Unattended backpack near a busy entrance

Learning Unit 3 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: An unattended backpack is found near a delivery entrance during shift change. No owner can be identified, people are walking nearby and a driver offers to move the bag away from the door.

Training visual: maintain distance, redirect people and notify control.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Place the immediate life-safety actions in the correct order.

State what must not be done by unqualified personnel.

Prepare a concise notification and identify observations for the later report.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Prevent anyone from touching, moving, opening, covering or closely examining the article.

Create distance, direct people through the approved safe route and control access without unnecessary approach.

Notify control, the supervisor and emergency services through approved channels, following restrictions on radio or phone use near the object.

From a safe position, record the exact location, appearance, time found, nearby activity, witnesses, actions and instructions received.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
Life safety and distance take priority over property and convenience.

The learner does not attempt to render the article harmless.

Information is concise, objective and suitable for specialist response.

Online reflection: How should crowd-control actions change if the normal exit passes close to the object?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 9: Break-in indicators discovered during patrol

Learning Unit 3 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: At 22:15, an officer finds a rear access door open, fresh marks near the lock and a failed perimeter light. No authorised work is recorded. A person without confirmed authority is walking away from the area.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Conduct a dynamic risk assessment and state the first radio report.

Explain containment, backup and safe contact with the person.

Identify possible evidence and the key occurrence-book facts.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Stop at a safe observation point, use cover, avoid entering alone and report location, observations, direction of travel and immediate hazards.

Request backup and supervisor support, control access and follow the approved incident or intrusion procedure.

Address the person only when safe and lawful, separating identity from authority and avoiding unsafe pursuit outside the officer's role.

Protect the door, tool marks, footprints, video and access records; record times, descriptions, communications, arrivals and handover.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner does not create a second victim or contaminate the scene.

Person and vehicle descriptions are objective and uncertainty is stated.

The record supports investigation, risk control and corrective action.

Online reflection: Which observation is a fact, which is an inference, and which still requires verification?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 10: Power failure and a suspicious help-desk call

Learning Unit 3 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A power interruption places the access-control system on backup. A caller claiming to be from technical support asks the control room to read out a system identifier and disable an alarm zone so remote repairs can begin. The caller's number is unfamiliar.

Training visual: use approved contingency records during a system disruption.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify the physical-security, information-security and continuity risks.

Explain how to verify the caller without using contact details supplied by the caller.

State the temporary controls, notifications and records required.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Do not disclose identifiers, credentials, alarm configuration or protected operating information and do not change systems on an unverified request.

Use the approved supplier or internal directory to contact the authorised technical function and verify the work request and change authority.

Apply the approved outage procedure: manual verification, controlled registers, additional staffing or patrols and clear handovers as authorised.

Preserve caller details and system logs, notify security management or the information-security contact, and record decisions and restoration checks.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner recognises social engineering during operational disruption.

Continuity controls preserve safety and an auditable access record.

System restoration is verified before temporary measures end.

Online reflection: Why do urgency and technical language make impersonation more convincing?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 11: Bribe offer and request to alter a register

Learning Unit 4 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: A regular delivery driver offers an officer cash to avoid a vehicle check and says everyone saves time this way. Later, a colleague asks the officer to change the occurrence-book time so the delay will not attract management attention.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Classify the conduct as poor practice, suspected misconduct, possible offence or more than one.

State the immediate response to the offer and the record-alteration request.

Identify evidence, confidential escalation and fair-process requirements.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Refuse the benefit, maintain the approved control and do not argue, threaten or create an unsafe confrontation.

Do not alter, erase or backdate the occurrence record; correct any genuine error transparently under the record-control procedure.

Report both approaches through the authorised confidential channel and preserve relevant video, messages, witness details and records.

Separate urgent access or credential restrictions from the disciplinary investigation and any criminal referral; do not predetermine guilt.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
Integrity is maintained and the access control is not bypassed.

Evidence is preserved without coordinating accounts.

The response respects confidentiality and fair procedure.

Online reflection: What should be recorded if refusing the bribe creates an immediate safety concern?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 12: Possible insider disclosure and confidential reporting

Learning Unit 4 | Workplace practice and online-learning activity

Situation: An officer sees a colleague photograph an access-control panel and send the image through a personal messaging application. The colleague says it is only for a technician and asks the officer not to create trouble by reporting it.

Training visual: discreetly report suspected misconduct through an authorised channel.

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify the protected-information and insider-risk indicators without assuming guilt.

Explain the safest immediate action and confidential reporting route.

State what evidence should be preserved and what must not be copied or shared further.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Do not accuse or conduct an unauthorised search; protect immediate access and information risks within current instructions.

Report promptly to the authorised security manager or confidential channel and request guidance on credential or device controls.

Record only facts personally observed, including time, location, device, words used and persons notified; identify available system or video records.

Do not forward the image, repeat rumours or discuss the allegation with unauthorised colleagues; preserve evidence through authorised processes.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner recognises a possible insider indicator and avoids prejudgment.

Protected information is not amplified during reporting.

Operational protection, evidence preservation and fair process remain separate but coordinated.

Online reflection: How can the organisation encourage early reporting without creating a culture of accusation?
