PRACTICAL SCENARIO 13: Unidentified drone observed near the site boundary

Learning Units 1 and 3 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: During an afternoon patrol, an officer sees a small drone repeatedly hovering outside a generic site boundary. Its operator is not visible. No prohibited item has been dropped and there is no confirmed attempt to enter the site.

Training visual: observe safely, report objectively and avoid unauthorised interference.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Patrol officer | Control-room operator | Security supervisor

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Separate observable facts from assumptions about the operator's purpose.

State the safe observation, notification and information-protection actions.

Prepare the first report and identify what must not be attempted by untrained staff.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Observe from a safe lawful position; note time, direction, altitude estimate, movement, duration and any visible features without leaving the assigned area.

Notify control and the authorised supervisor through the approved channel; apply the current site procedure and request police or other authorised support when the assessed risk requires it.

Do not chase, capture, interfere with or attempt to disable the drone unless a specific lawful authority, approved procedure and trained capability exist.

Protect operational information: do not post the sighting online or expose camera coverage, patrol patterns or sensitive areas while reporting.

Record observations, persons notified, instructions, subsequent sightings and the final handover or closure decision.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner avoids inventing powers or assuming hostile intent.

The report is objective, time-linked and useful to an authorised decision-maker.

The response protects people and information without revealing site vulnerabilities.

Online reflection: Which details are useful for identification without disclosing protected operational information?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 14: Severe rain makes the normal evacuation route unsafe

Learning Units 1 and 3 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: Heavy rain causes local flooding across the normal pedestrian evacuation route. An alarm requires part of a fictional campus to evacuate, but several people begin walking toward the waterlogged route because it is the route they know.

Training visual: redirect people from a route made unsafe by severe weather.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Access officer | Control-room operator | Evacuation marshal

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Set the immediate life-safety priorities and define who may change the route.

Give a concise radio report and clear public instruction.

Explain how access security, accountability and post-incident records continue during evacuation.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Prevent entry into the unsafe area and direct people to the approved alternative route; never require anyone to cross moving or uncertain-depth water.

Notify control of the blocked route, exact safe access point, people affected and support required; obtain confirmation of the temporary route from the authorised emergency structure.

Use calm, repeated instructions and reasonable assistance for persons who need support, without causing crowding at the control point.

Maintain essential perimeter and access controls unless the emergency plan directs otherwise; do not create informal shortcuts through restricted areas.

Complete roll-call, outstanding-person, route-change and incident records, and link corrective action to the emergency-plan review.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
Life safety takes priority while lawful control is maintained.

The changed route is authorised, communicated and recorded.

The learner includes assistance, accountability and recovery actions.

Online reflection: What information would allow control to decide whether more staff or emergency services are needed?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 15: Lost credential followed by an attempted tailgate

Learning Units 2 and 3 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: An employee reports a lost access card. Minutes later, a person in similar clothing asks a colleague to hold a controlled door open, saying the card was left at home and an urgent meeting has started.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Security officer | Employee host | Access-control supervisor

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify immediate credential and access-control actions.

Demonstrate a respectful identity-and-authority verification conversation.

List the electronic and written records that should be preserved.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Keep the door controlled and prevent tailgating without physical confrontation; explain that familiarity or urgency cannot replace verification.

Report and disable or suspend the missing credential through the authorised process, noting the effective time and decision-maker.

Verify the person's identity and current access authority through approved records and a trusted contact method, not through information supplied only by the person.

If temporary access is authorised, apply the approved credential, escort, area and time limits and communicate them clearly.

Preserve access logs, relevant video references, the lost-card report, verification result, access decision and final credential disposition.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
No access is granted solely on appearance, status or urgency.

The missing credential and attempted access are linked in the audit trail.

The response remains respectful and non-discriminatory.

Online reflection: Why must the missing-card time be recorded accurately?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 16: Caller claims emergency technical authority

Learning Units 3 and 4 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: During a system fault, a caller claims to be from technical support and says a safety manager has approved urgent remote work. The caller asks for an alarm identifier, controller details and temporary disabling of a protective function.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Control-room officer | Caller | Duty supervisor

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify the social-engineering indicators and protected information.

State a safe verification and continuity response.

Explain what digital and physical evidence should be preserved.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Do not disclose system details, credentials, identifiers or operational configuration and do not alter protective settings on an incoming caller's instruction.

Use a separately verified service contact and approved change-authorisation process to confirm identity, scope, timing and decision-maker.

Apply the approved manual or degraded-mode procedure, request additional patrol or access support if required and communicate only the minimum operational information.

Preserve the call time, number displayed, words used, requested action, verification attempts, system alerts and related occurrence or help-desk references.

Escalate suspected fraud, attempted unauthorised access or cybercrime through the authorised incident route; security staff preserve and report rather than conduct an unauthorised investigation.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner verifies through an independent channel.

Continuity controls remain active during the fault.

The record supports both operational and technical review.

Online reflection: Which details may be shared with verified support, and who authorises that disclosure?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 17: Visitor becomes verbally aggressive after access is refused

Learning Unit 3 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: A visitor's appointment cannot be confirmed. The visitor raises their voice, moves closer to the desk and accuses the officer of discrimination. Other visitors begin watching and recording on phones.

Training visual: calm communication, safe distance and early support.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Access officer | Visitor | Supervisor or witness officer

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Demonstrate a dignity-based de-escalation conversation.

State the safety threshold for requesting support or changing position.

Prepare an objective record that avoids labels and unsupported conclusions.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Maintain safe distance and an open posture, use a calm tone and state the access requirement and available next step without arguing about motive.

Ask one clear question at a time, acknowledge the concern without admitting facts not established and offer the approved host-verification or complaint route.

Position yourself so that an exit and assistance remain available; request a supervisor or additional officer early if proximity, threats, crowding or behaviour increases risk.

Use only lawful, necessary and proportionate measures if immediate safety requires intervention; stop restrictions when the need ends.

Record exact words or actions where material, distances and movements observed, assistance requested, instructions given and outcome; do not use insulting or diagnostic labels.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner communicates the rule and options clearly.

Safety measures are proportionate to observed behaviour.

The report distinguishes allegation, observation and decision.

Online reflection: What could the officer say to explain the rule without escalating the disagreement?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 18: CCTV clip is shared through an unauthorised messaging group

Learning Unit 4 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: A short clip showing a security incident is forwarded to officers through a private messaging group. The sender says it will help identify a person. The original export source, authorisation and retention status are unknown.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Receiving officer | Control-room custodian | Security manager

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Identify the confidentiality, privacy and evidence risks.

State what the receiving officer should do without spreading the clip further.

Describe the authorised preservation and disclosure record.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Do not forward, edit, annotate or publish the clip and do not use an uncontrolled copy as the sole basis for operational action.

Report receipt confidentially to the authorised manager or information custodian and preserve the message details without unnecessary further copying.

Ask the authorised system custodian to preserve the original recording, export log, date and time basis, camera reference, access history and retention hold under the approved process.

Limit viewing and disclosure to authorised persons with a lawful operational purpose; use the minimum necessary information and an approved transfer channel.

Record who supplied, received, accessed, preserved and transferred the material, plus any instruction, incident reference and final disposition.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner protects privacy and the integrity of the original record.

Unauthorised circulation stops without destroying evidence.

Disclosure is purpose-limited and auditable.

Online reflection: Why can a useful-looking clip still be unreliable evidence?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 19: Incomplete shift handover leaves unresolved risks

Learning Units 1, 2 and 3 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: At shift change, the outgoing team reports a recurring alarm fault, a radio with a weak battery and a key-pouch count that has not been reconciled. The occurrence book contains brief notes but no owner, due time or escalation reference.

Training visual: verify records, keys, radios and unresolved actions at handover.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Outgoing officer | Incoming officer | Shift supervisor

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Conduct a structured handover and identify what cannot be accepted as complete.

Assign immediate controls, owners and escalation times.

Complete the records needed for accountability and later closure.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Verify staffing, post status, access restrictions, open incidents, keys, credentials, radios, protective systems and pending visitors or contractors against the controlled handover checklist.

Treat the key discrepancy as unresolved until reconciled or escalated; apply the approved restriction, search and replacement-control process without altering records.

Place the weak radio on charge or replace it through the equipment register and confirm that every post retains an effective communication method.

Apply the authorised contingency for the alarm fault, link the fault and incident references and assign a named owner, priority, due time and review point.

Both officers and the supervisor record the status accepted, exceptions, controls, notifications and items requiring follow-up; closure requires evidence, not only a signature.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
The learner verifies rather than merely receives a verbal handover.

Every exception has a control, owner and review time.

Equipment and key accountability are traceable.

Online reflection: Which unresolved item creates the greatest immediate risk, and why?

PRACTICAL SCENARIO 20: Possible cable tampering and service disruption

Learning Units 3 and 4 | Advanced role-play and online-learning activity

Situation: During patrol after a local power interruption, an officer sees a damaged service-box cover, fresh tool marks and cut cable near an external boundary. An unfamiliar vehicle is moving away, but no person is currently at the damaged point.

lessons.title: ROLE-PLAY ROLES
lessons.html: Patrol officer | Control-room operator | Police or technical liaison

lessons.title: LEARNER TASK
lessons.html:
Set the safety perimeter and decide what must not be touched.

Give a concise report without pursuing or confronting the vehicle.

Identify evidence, continuity and external-notification records.

lessons.title: MODEL RESPONSE
lessons.html:
Assume electrical, fire or other technical danger until a qualified person confirms safety; keep people away and do not handle cables, covers or tools.

Notify control with the exact generic location, hazards, observed damage, vehicle description and direction of travel; do not leave the assigned duty to pursue.

Request police, emergency or authorised technical response through the approved plan and implement power-loss, access and communications contingencies.

Protect the wider scene and likely approach or departure paths from contamination; preserve authorised video, access, alarm and maintenance references.

Record observations, times, notifications, instructions, service impact, evidence handover and corrective-action owner while avoiding unsupported claims about identity or offence.

lessons.title: ASSESSMENT EVIDENCE
lessons.html:
Technical danger is controlled before evidence handling.

The learner reports useful vehicle facts without unsafe pursuit.

Operational continuity and evidence preservation are coordinated.

Online reflection: What facts may be reported immediately even though criminal intent has not been proved?

SKILL STATION 1: Pre-shift readiness and controlled briefing

Objective: Demonstrate that the officer, post, information, equipment and unresolved risks are ready before duty begins.

lessons.title: PROCEDURE
lessons.html:
Confirm current appointment, post allocation, fitness for duty and required licence or credential status.

Verify the controlled post order, security-plan extract, temporary instructions and effective dates; remove or report obsolete copies.

Receive a structured handover covering open incidents, access restrictions, visitors, contractors, keys, systems, patrol exceptions and escalation points.

Function-check the radio, panic or duress device, torch, protective equipment and recording tools without exposing codes or sensitive settings.

Record defects, temporary controls, owner and review time; do not accept a post when a critical control is absent and no authorised contingency exists.

Facilitator provides three defects: one equipment defect, one outdated instruction and one unresolved incident.

Learner gives a two-minute briefing-back and states whether the post is ready, ready with restrictions or not ready.

A peer challenges one decision; the learner must identify the authority and evidence supporting the response.

SKILL STATION 2: Access-control conversation and decision record

Objective: Apply identity, authority and access conditions while maintaining dignity and a complete audit trail.

lessons.html:
State your role and the applicable access requirement in plain language.

Ask for identity and purpose, then separately verify appointment, authority, area and time conditions.

Use an approved independent contact or system; do not rely only on information supplied by the visitor.

Decide: grant, grant with conditions, delay, refuse or refer. Explain the next approved step without arguing or making threats.

Escalate when authority, behaviour, information or risk changes, then record the facts, verification, decision and outcome.

lessons.title: PRACTICE ACTIVITY
lessons.html:
Role-play a contractor who is known to staff but absent from the appointment list.

Repeat the role-play with a language barrier or hearing difficulty and provide reasonable communication support.

Write a six-line occurrence-book entry that separates observation, information received and the final decision.

SKILL STATION 3: Initial radio report and incident update

Objective: Give a concise report that lets control understand the location, hazard, people, actions and support required.

lessons.html:
Prepare before transmitting: identify the channel, call sign, urgency and minimum information required.

State the exact approved location reference and immediate hazard first.

Report only observed facts and clearly attribute information received from another person.

State people affected, actions already taken and the specific support or decision required.

Listen for read-back or instruction, confirm critical details and record the transmission time and outcome.

lessons.title: PRACTICE ACTIVITY
lessons.html:
Give a 30-second initial report for Scenario 14, 17 or 20.

After the facilitator changes one fact, give a short update without repeating irrelevant information.

Write the matching occurrence-book entry and compare it with the audio or facilitator notes.

SKILL STATION 4: Incident report - fact, source and inference

Objective: Produce a fair, chronological report that another authorised person can understand and verify.

lessons.title: PROCEDURE
lessons.html:
Write the date, time, location, assignment and how the incident came to your attention.

Record what you directly saw, heard or did in chronological order using neutral language.

Attribute information from others by naming or describing the authorised source and recording the words accurately where material.

Label any inference or assessment and state the facts supporting it; do not present suspicion as proved fact.

Record instructions, decisions, notifications, evidence references, outcome and outstanding action. Correct errors transparently; never erase, overwrite or backdate.

Objective: Protect possible physical or digital evidence without exceeding authority or contaminating the record.

lessons.title: PROCEDURE
lessons.html:
Make the area safe and prevent unnecessary access, handling, viewing, copying or alteration.

Identify the lawful reason and authorised decision for taking control, preserving a record or refusing access.

Record the item's or record's original location, condition, identifying features, date, time and person who discovered it.

Use approved packaging, seals, export procedures and labels only when trained and authorised; never place protected details in a public or general-purpose channel.

Record every transfer: giver, receiver, date, time, purpose, condition, seal or reference and destination. Obtain acknowledgement and report any break in continuity.

TermMeaning
AuthorisedPermitted by current law, a valid appointment, delegation or approved procedure.
Critical infrastructureInfrastructure considered or declared under the Critical Infrastructure Protection Act framework.

National Key Point (NKP)A place or area declared under the applicable National Key Points legislation.
NecessityThe requirement that an action is genuinely needed to achieve a lawful purpose.

SAQASouth African Qualifications Authority.

options.label: C

options.label: C

options.text: an officer may exercise any site-related authority anywhere in South Africa.

options.label: D

questions.question: Before disclosing protected information, the officer should:

options.label: A
options.text: send all available information so the recipient can choose what is useful.

options.label: C
options.text: use a private messaging group because it is faster.

options.label: D
options.text: remove the date and then publish the information.

options.label: A
options.text: dismiss the employee immediately in every case.

options.label: B
options.text: ignore the operational risk until the hearing is completed.

options.label: C
options.text: publish the allegation so witnesses can respond.

options.label: D
options.text: control the immediate risk, preserve evidence and follow the authorised fair process without prejudging the outcome.

questions.question: An objective occurrence-book entry should contain:

options.label: A
options.text: facts, attributed information, decisions, times, notifications and transparent corrections.

options.label: B
options.text: labels such as 'criminal' whenever access is refused.

options.label: C
options.text: only the final outcome.

options.label: D
options.text: unverified rumours if they appear important.

questions.question: A caller claiming to be technical support asks for alarm identifiers and temporary disabling of a protective function. The officer should:

options.label: A
options.text: provide the information if the caller sounds confident.

options.label: B
options.text: disable the function and verify the caller afterwards.

options.label: C
options.text: refuse disclosure or alteration, verify through an independent approved contact and use the authorised change process.

options.label: D
options.text: transfer the call to another officer without reporting it.

questions.question: An unidentified drone is repeatedly observed near a generic site boundary. The officer should:

options.label: A
options.text: attempt to disable it with available equipment.

options.label: B
options.text: observe safely, report objective details, protect operational information and follow authorised procedure.

options.label: C
options.text: post a photograph online to locate the operator.

options.label: D
options.text: leave the assigned area to chase it.

questions.question: Flooding makes the normal evacuation route unsafe. The officer should:

options.label: A
options.text: continue using the route because it appears on the old plan.

options.label: B
options.text: create an unapproved shortcut through a restricted area.

options.label: C
options.text: wait for people to discover the hazard themselves.

options.label: D
options.text: block the unsafe route, direct people to an approved alternative and report the change to control.

questions.question: A CCTV clip is shared in an unauthorised messaging group. The receiving officer should:

options.label: A
options.text: stop further circulation, report receipt confidentially and have the authorised custodian preserve the original recording and audit trail.

options.label: B
options.text: forward it only to trusted friends.

options.label: C
options.text: edit the clip to make the person easier to identify.

options.label: D
options.text: delete every trace before reporting it.

Document control and marking principles
Confidentiality: Do not issue this memorandum to learners before the assessment and feedback process authorised by the provider. Store and transmit it through approved controlled channels.
General marking rules
Award marks for correct principles expressed in the learner's own words; exact wording is not required unless the question asks for a specific test or sequence.
Accept a lawful equivalent response supported by current legislation, an approved site procedure or a verified delegated instruction. Record the accepted alternative for moderation.
Do not award a mark for an answer that invents authority, relies on bias, exposes protected information or recommends an unsafe action.
Where one sentence contains several distinct correct points, allocate only the marks supported by the marking indicators.
Use the approved assessment plan for competence thresholds, reassessment and integrated practical evidence. A written score alone does not prove practical competence.
Assessment blueprint
Section A memorandum [20 marks]
Allocation: One mark for each correct answer. No half marks. Section total: 20.
Section B memorandum [40 marks]
Question 21 [6 marks]
Differentiate the functions of the Minister or delegated authority from the responsibilities of the owner or person in control. Give three points for each role.
Minister/delegated authority: exercises only current statutory functions; issues lawful notices, directions, standards or delegations through prescribed processes; receives information or oversees compliance where authorised and coordinates with responsible state structures. Award any three relevant points. (3)
Owner/person in control: establishes and maintains the approved policy and security plan; provides competent staff, supervision, equipment and facilities; controls access; maintains incident and assurance systems; reviews risks and corrects deficiencies. Award any three relevant points. (3)
Question 22 [5 marks]
List five records that demonstrate that the owner is maintaining an effective safeguarding system.
Any five: approved policy/security plan/post orders and version history; appointment/screening/competence records; induction/refresher records; equipment/key/credential registers; occurrence books/patrol records/incident reports; escalation logs; inspection/exercise findings; corrective-action and management-review records. (1 each)
Question 23 [5 marks]
State five controls required before a person may be deployed under a lawful provisional appointment.
Award one mark each for any five: confirmed lawful basis; written appointment and authorised decision-maker; restricted duties; direct supervision; recorded outstanding checks; required training/induction; review date; controlled access/credential limits; no unrestricted deployment. (5)
Question 24 [6 marks]
Describe the safe decision sequence when an unidentified or unauthorised person requests entry.
Observe from a safe position and assess immediate danger. (1)
Identify yourself and request identity, purpose and authority where safe and lawful. (1)
Verify through the approved independent access-control process. (1)
Keep access controlled while authority is unconfirmed. (1)
Explain the decision and approved next step calmly. (1)
Escalate when risk, refusal, suspected crime or uncertainty requires it, and record the event. (1)
Question 25 [4 marks]
Explain what an officer must do when consent is withdrawn during a consent-based search.
Stop the consent-based search unless a separate lawful authority clearly applies. (1)
Do not use force merely to complete that search. (1)
Apply the lawful access consequence and consult the authorised supervisor. (1)
Record the withdrawal, response, persons consulted and outcome. (1)
Question 26 [5 marks]
Explain five actions that protect the integrity and chain of custody of possible evidence.
Any five: protect safety and prevent unnecessary handling; record original location/condition/features; identify lawful authority; use approved packaging/seal when trained; preserve digital originals and access logs; record every transfer; obtain receiver acknowledgement; report breaks in continuity; deliver promptly to the authorised custodian. (1 each)
Question 27 [4 marks]
Explain why the same conduct can be both workplace misconduct and a criminal offence, and why the employment outcome must not be prejudged.
Conduct may breach employment duties and also meet elements of a statutory offence; the two processes have different purposes and decision-makers. (2)
Immediate risk may justify temporary post removal, but guilt/dismissal must follow the authorised fair process, verified facts and applicable labour requirements. (2)
Question 28 [5 marks]
List the five questions in the authorised-disclosure test used before protected information is shared.
Is there a lawful duty or authority to disclose? (1)
Is the recipient authorised and is the information required for a legitimate purpose? (1)
Can the purpose be achieved by sharing less information? (1)
Is the channel approved and secure? (1)
Must the disclosure be recorded or reported? (1)
Section C memorandum [40 marks]
Question 29: Lost credential, attempted tailgating and escalating behaviour [20 marks]
Scenario: An employee reports a lost access card. Ten minutes later, a person wearing the same department's uniform asks a colleague to hold a controlled door open. The person says an urgent meeting has started, cannot produce another credential and becomes verbally aggressive when the officer keeps the door controlled.
a) [5 marks]
Keep the door controlled and prevent tailgating without confrontation.
Report and suspend/disable the lost credential through the authorised process.
Verify identity and current authority independently.
Request supervisor/support early as behaviour escalates.
Maintain safe distance, exit route and protection of other people.
b) [4 marks]
State the access requirement and role calmly.
Acknowledge urgency/concern without admitting unverified facts.
Ask one clear question at a time and explain the approved next step.
Avoid threats, labels, discriminatory language or argument.
c) [5 marks]
Lost-card report and effective disablement time.
Access-control and credential audit logs.
Appointment/authority verification result.
Relevant CCTV reference preserved by an authorised custodian.
Occurrence-book/incident entry recording words, behaviour, decisions, notifications and outcome.
d) [6 marks]
No access solely on clothing, familiarity or urgency: verify first. (2)
No unlawful search, detention or force because a person is argumentative: escalate and use only lawful proportionate safety measures. (2)
Escalate threats, crowding, suspected crime, unclear authority or safety risk to the supervisor/police as appropriate and record the response. (2)
Critical review: Do not treat a high total as sufficient if the response grants access without verification, uses unlawful force or search, disables a protective function without authority, circulates protected information or contaminates evidence. Follow the approved assessment plan for critical criteria and reassessment.
Question 30: System fault, social engineering and protected information [20 marks]
Scenario: During an access-control system fault, a caller claims to be emergency technical support. The caller asks for controller details and temporary disabling of an alarm. At the same time, a colleague sends a CCTV clip of the fault area to a private messaging group and says it may help technicians.
a) [6 marks]
Do not disclose identifiers, credentials or system details.
Do not disable or alter protection on the incoming caller's instruction.
Record the call time, number displayed, words used and requested action.
Verify identity and authority using a separately verified approved contact.
Use the approved change-authorisation process.
Notify the duty supervisor/control and escalate suspected fraud or cybercrime through the authorised route.
b) [4 marks]
Apply the approved manual/degraded-mode procedure.
Maintain controlled entry and movement.
Deploy additional patrol/access staff if authorised and required.
Record temporary controls, responsible persons and review/restore time.
c) [6 marks]
Do not forward, edit or publish the clip.
Report the unauthorised sharing confidentially.
Preserve the original recording through the authorised system custodian.
Preserve export/access logs, camera reference and time basis.
Preserve message and call metadata without unnecessary copying.
Limit viewing/transfer to authorised persons through an approved channel and record every access/transfer.
d) [4 marks]
No investigative or system-administration power unless specifically appointed, trained and authorised.
No disclosure beyond lawful purpose and minimum necessary information.
No alteration of protective controls without approved authority.
No public/general-purpose sharing of protected records; preserve and report instead.
Critical review: Do not treat a high total as sufficient if the response grants access without verification, uses unlawful force or search, disables a protective function without authority, circulates protected information or contaminates evidence. Follow the approved assessment plan for critical criteria and reassessment.

Moderation checks
Question paper and memorandum versions match.
Mark totals and transfers have been recalculated.
Equivalent answers were accepted consistently and recorded.
Unsafe or unlawful reasoning was handled according to the approved critical-criteria rule.
Feedback and reassessment decisions are specific, fair and traceable.
Learner and site information is protected in retained evidence.
